texts: mixed: the eleven-lantern group, its count, the day/year terms and the per-lantern distribution of both 'relit' and the dim burning all come through, but the tense on 'relit' is lost — a participle sitting in front of a noun takes no tense in our instruction set, so the parse says the lanterns are relit without saying the relighting had already happened. Rewrite as 'On day 17 of Year 1, the eleven lanterns of the Middle Row had been relit, and they burned dimly.' so the relighting becomes its own past event ordered before the burning.

good. 'The dim lanterns' is resolved back to the same eleven lanterns, 'dim' is distributed to each of them, and the giving is carried both as a group event and per lantern with the weak mist-light as what is given.
good. the attracting event, the mist-light as its agent, and the 'a handful' nightmoth group with its nightmoth/moth genus are all covered.

mixed: the value twelve and the 'that night' day terms come through, but 'the moth-count at the Middle Row' forces the parse to place the tally itself spatially inside the Middle Row — an abstract count has no licensed way to carry a place — and a bare-numeral copular predicate gives the time modifier nothing of its own to attach to. Rewrite as 'Twelve nightmoths were counted at the Middle Row that night.' — the counting is then an event that can carry both the place and the time, and the number rides the moth group.
good. the fall of the thread harvest is carried as a past event with the harvest as the thing that fell; no baseline figure is stated and none is invented.

mixed: both collectors, the shared thread group, the Middle Row as source and the 'next morning' date (day 18 of Year 1, ordered after the count) are all right, but bare 'few' has no carrier — our instruction set reads 'few' as a proportion word for generic claims and lists only 'a few' among the vague counts, so the scarcity you intend may not survive. Rewrite as 'Pell and Coraline Ash collected a handful of silken threads from the Middle Row the next morning.' (a licensed vague count), and if the point is that the take was smaller than usual, state that in its own clause.
good. Hesper, the threads, the sea-water, Cauldron Hall and the 'that day' date (day 18) are all carried on one boiling event.

bad: 'instead of three' is lost — nothing records that three vessels was the expected yield — and the parse also invents content the sentence never states: it places the cauldrons at Cauldron Hall (only the boiling is located there) and invents a measurement scale for 'two vessels'. Rewrite as 'The cauldrons yielded two vessels of mire-essence, but three vessels were expected.' so the expectation becomes its own clause tied to the yield by 'but'; the two invented atoms are translator-side slips a rewrite cannot reach.
